Prototype

PRO-tuh-type — starts with 'proto,' meaning first; a prototype is the very first typed-out version. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Prototype is an original or first model of something, built to test a design before it is produced in large numbers.

The engineering team built three different prototypes before settling on a final design for the drone.

Worked Example

A shoe company designs a new running shoe. Before ordering a hundred thousand pairs, they build just a handful, hand them to test runners, and gather feedback on comfort and durability.

That small handful of test shoes, built to check the design before mass production, is the prototype. Unlike 'sample,' which can just mean any small example pulled from a finished batch, a prototype comes before mass production even begins.

How Prototype Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

model: a version built to represent or test a design

Antonyms

replica

replica: an exact copy of a finished original

finished product

finished product: a completed item ready for sale or use

How Strong Is It? — sketch → prototype → production model

sketch vs. prototype

sketch vs. prototype: A sketch is weaker than a prototype — a sketch is just a rough drawing of an idea, while a prototype is an actual built, testable model of the design.

production model vs. prototype

production model vs. prototype: A production model is a step beyond a prototype: a prototype is built to test and refine a design, but a production model is the finalized version that gets mass-manufactured.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — proto-

prefix — proto-: first (Greek)

root — -type

root — -type: mold, model, impression (Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Greek protos (first) plus typos (mold, impression) literally means 'first impression' or 'first model.' A prototype is the first shaped version of a design, made before all the later copies.
